items: [normalize] in an absolute path `..` at the root is dropped and the leading `/` stays
[normalize] in a relative path an unmatched `..` is kept, and a later `..` does not remove it
[normalize] a trailing `/` survives dot-segment removal when the input had one
[Edge cases] no trailing `/` is added to a result of `/` or `.`
[Edge cases] an empty result is `/` for absolute input and `.` for relative (the empty string gives `.`)
